questions.stem: A four-year-old boy with a history of waddling gait, larger than normal calves and frequent falls receives a spontaneously breathing volatile-based anaesthetic with sevoflurane. questions.stem: Infection control management of patients with carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (CPE) infection should include all of the following EXCEPT

opts.t: Contact precautions with gloves and gowns
opts.why: Incorrect as the EXCEPT response: Contact precautions are central to control of CPE/CRO transmission.

opts.t: Routine droplet precautions as the sole transmission precaution

opts.why: Incorrect as the EXCEPT response: Environmental and shared-device contamination is an established transmission route.

questions.expl: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales spread largely by contact and contaminated environments. Contact precautions, dedicated equipment and patient placement are recommended; droplet precautions alone are not sufficient as the routine organism-specific strategy.

questions.expl: Renal tubular acidosis usually causes normal-anion-gap hyperchloraemic acidosis, whereas lactate, uraemic organic anions and salicylates raise the gap.

questions.stem: A patient with C6 tetraplegia is undergoing removal of bladder stones under general anaesthesia. The blood pressure rises to 166/88 mmHg. The appropriate response is to

opts.t: Allow sustained extreme hypertension without intervention
Deepen anaesthesia and promptly treat autonomic dysreflexia

questions.expl: Noxious stimuli below a high spinal cord lesion provoke autonomic dysreflexia; remove trigger, deepen anaesthesia and control marked hypertension.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man is brought into the Emergency Department four hours after an accidental chemical exposure during crop spraying. questions.expl: Organophosphate pesticide exposure inhibits cholinesterases, producing cholinergic toxicity and prolonged suxamethonium paralysis.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with no past history of ischaemic heart disease is three days post-total hip replacement surgery. questions.expl: Ischaemic chest symptoms and a troponin rise above the 99th percentile satisfy myocardial infarction criteria despite no ST elevation.
questions.note: An isolated postoperative troponin rise can also be termed MINS; symptoms make the NSTEMI classification plausible.

questions.stem: A 100 kg 32-year-old male presents two hours after suffering a 30% total body surface area electrical burn. He has had no resuscitation fluids. The infusion rate of isotonic crystalloid resuscitation fluid required for this man for the next six hours is
